description: The calls each MCP tool makes as the guardian, and the permission each call needs: the least privileged one that the API's docs list (docs/tool-permissions.md, NFR1). The executor is not a tool, but it acts as the guardian too, so its calls are here as well. Each permission names its API, as in agent-permissions.json. type is application (an app-only token) or delegated (the OBO token, with the approver's rights). Nothing reads this file at run time: a unit test checks it against the calls the code makes and against the grants (tests/unit/mcp_server/test_tool_permissions.py).

scan_registry.why: the agent identities, with their sponsors (the orphan check)
each agent's own app role assignments (the over-permissioned check)
the app role assignments each agent inherits from its blueprint
the role names of each API that an agent holds roles on
the blueprints and their credentials (the expiring check)
the sign-ins of the last 30 days (the dormant check)
the findings, into the audit log
the latest disable request for each dormant agent

get_agent.why: one agent identity, by its app ID

submit_disable_agent_request.why: the agent and the guardian: not the guardian's own, and not disabled yet
the disable request, for an approver

executor.why: the request: approved, and by this approver?
the same checks as the request tool, and the agent's object ID for the write
claim the request, right before the write
the disable, with the approver's rights
read accountEnabled back, until Graph shows the change
